question: Which Indian river was added to the National River Conservation Plan in 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Musi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Musi River, located in Telangana, was added to the National River Conservation Plan (NRCP) in 2024.
 
• The NRCP is an initiative by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) to conserve and rejuvenate polluted rivers across India.
 
• The Musi River flows through Hyderabad and has been heavily polluted due to untreated sewage, industrial waste, and urban runoff.
 
• Under the NRCP, measures such as sewage treatment plants, bio-remediation, riverbank restoration, and public awareness campaigns are implemented to revive polluted rivers.
 
• The inclusion of the Musi River in the NRCP aims to address environmental concerns and improve water quality for better ecological and human health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yamuna River:**

 
 
• The Yamuna River is the largest tributary of the Ganga and flows through several states, including Uttarakhand, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• It has been part of the NRCP since 1993 due to high pollution levels in cities like Delhi and Agra.
 
• Under the NRCP, projects such as sewage treatment, riverfront development, and waste management have been undertaken.
 
 
 
• **Krishna River:**
 
 
• The Krishna River is one of India's major rivers, flowing through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is known for its importance in irrigation, hydroelectric power generation, and water supply.
 
• The Krishna is not part of the NRCP, as pollution levels are comparatively lower than rivers like the Yamuna or Musi.
 
 
 
• **Gomti River:**
 
 
• The Gomti River flows through Uttar Pradesh, including the city of Lucknow.
 
• It has been part of the NRCP since the late 1990s due to pollution from untreated sewage and industrial effluents.
 
• Efforts under the NRCP include constructing sewage treatment plants and reducing pollution sources.
